title: The BMW R 1300 GS disappears: what will be its replacement? - Modernet Digital
content:
The BMW R 1300 GS disappears from the official list for the 2027 lineup, and this has put fans of the German brand on alert. BMW’s best-selling trail bike seems ready to make way for a new model with an updated boxer engine. Many wonder if this absence is just an aesthetic change or the beginning of a completely new era for the GS family. In any case, the news leaves no one indifferent and raises great expectations. The disappearance of the R 1300 GS in the 2027 lineup update is an unusual fact that attracts the attention of BMW followers. The BMW GS models, especially the 1300, have been one of the commercial pillars of BMW Motorrad for years, being one of the best-selling trail bikes in Europe. That is why its absence in the annual renewal is more than just a simple oversight. Besides the R 1300 GS, the R 1300 GS Adventure and the F 900 GS and F 450 GS also do not appear in the new lineup. The latter is new, so its absence has a logical explanation, but the rest do not. Rumors about a new BMW R 1350 GS are not new, but the confirmation that the R 1300 GS disappears reinforces this theory. The boxer engine is the icon of the GS family, and its evolution has marked the different generations: from the R 1200 GS to the current R 1300 GS. The new 1350 could represent an important leap in performance and technology. There is no official confirmation yet, but the absence of the R 1300 GS in the 2027 lineup suggests that BMW is working on a replacement that could arrive in the short term. But not everything is uncertainty: while the R 1300 GS is absent, BMW has updated other models in its 2027 lineup. Models such as the R 1300 R and R 1300 RS receive new luggage racks and improved Touring packages. The F 900 R and XR incorporate the M Endurance chain in some trims, and the K 1600 debuts a new Imperial Blue metallic color. The BMW M 1000 RR features a new third-generation M Motorsport chassis, lighter and more flexible, and forged wheels as standard. The M 1000 R and XR replace the Competition package with the new M Track packages. In short, the combination of absence and updates in other models reinforces the idea that BMW is preparing a major move for its flagship trail bike. The future of the BMW GS is full of mystery, but the possible arrival of the R 1350 GS with a renewed boxer engine makes any enthusiast eagerly await what’s coming. Many questions will only be answered with time: whether it is a simple renewal or a new era for BMW Motorrad, but one thing is clear—the GS will remain a protagonist in terms of innovation and passion for two-wheeled adventure. The BMW R 1300 GS has been a symbol for years, and the new 1350 seems destined to continue this legend with a boxer engine that promises more power and technology. title: Rentokil Initial plc (LON:RTO) stock rises after Goldman Sachs Group Inc (NYSE:GS) upgrade as U.S. pest recovery becomes price test - Bez Kabli
content: Rentokil Initial plc (LON:RTO) rose on Tuesday after Goldman Sachs Group Inc NYSE:GS upgraded the stock, but the bigger number for shareholders is the target gap. At 590p, Goldman’s new target is about 30% above the after-close London quote and 16% above the 507p year high shown by AJ Bell. At 21:02 BST, London trading had ended. Hargreaves Lansdown showed Rentokil at 454.60p bid and 454.80p offer; AJ Bell showed a session high of 458.20p and volume of 10.6 million shares. The upgrade hit a stock that had just been sitting on its long-term line. A London Stock Exchange/FTSE Russell tearsheet dated July 6 put Rentokil at 4.45 pounds, equal to its 200-day average, below its 50-day average of 4.59 pounds, and down 16% over five years against a 43.1% rise for the FTSE 350. Goldman analyst Suhasini Varanasi, listed by Rentokil as the bank’s covering analyst, upgraded the shares to Buy from Neutral. Sharecast reported Goldman’s view that North American organic growth, which began to turn in the third quarter of 2025, can reach mid-single digits by 2027. That is why the broker note matters. North America produced $995 million of Rentokil’s $1.68 billion first-quarter revenue, or 59%. Its 3.9% organic growth is better than the weak period that hurt the stock before, but still 2.7 percentage points below Rollins’ first-quarter organic growth. The Rollins figure is group-level, so it is not a perfect match, but it is the peer yardstick Goldman cited. Goldman’s case does not require Rentokil to catch Rollins at once. It requires investors to believe the North America number can move toward mid-single digits as Terminix disruption fades and branch, sales and marketing work starts to show up in revenue. Investing.com reported Goldman also expects group EBITA margin to rise to 17.1% in 2027. Rentokil Chief Executive Mike Duffy called the first quarter “a good start” and cited “continued momentum” in North America. The same update showed North America colleague retention at 82.6% and customer retention at 80.4%, two operating data points investors will watch before paying for the Goldman target. Rentokil Initial Rentokil also put a new executive on the U.S. problem. It named Rafael “Rafa” Carrasco as CEO, North America, from Aug. 3. Duffy called him the “ideal leader” for the unit; Carrasco said his focus would be “operational excellence.” Rentokil Initial Chief Financial Officer Paul Edgecliffe-Johnson told the April call he wanted Rentokil to become “a nice, safe, boring stock.” The Goldman upgrade puts that aim next to a growth target. Investing The next dated test is July 30, when Rentokil is due to publish interim results. The company lists its third-quarter trading update for Oct. 22. title: Karol G’s Bikini Top Peeks Through See-Through Natalia Fedner Chain Top - AOL.com
content: Karol G always knows just how to make her mark with unique fashion statements. Keeping up with this, Karol turned the 52nd American Music Awards into her personal runway in a daring Natalia Fedner look that was, honestly, impossible to ignore. The celebrated superstar stepped onto the carpet in a completely see-through copper-toned chain top layered over a tiny black string bikini top. This risqué piece was further paired with an oversized, voluminous black skirt that dramatically balanced the barely-there upper half. The whole look screamed all things bold and beautiful. For the star-studded occasion, Karol G chose to wear an all-black Natalia Fedner look. It was just the most chic and unique choice for the occasion. This featured a metallic mesh top, which clung to her frame like liquid armor. Karol’s statement-worthy top featured a rather distressed chain detailing, which took it to the next level. It also had beautifully placed drapes, shredded edges, and strategically draped cutouts. These clearly exposed her toned midriff and bikini straps underneath, adding a rather fiery and fabulous twist to the whole look. Further, Karol also styled the statement-making ensemble with beachy wet-look waves, which made her face look insanely beautiful. Karol also chose to go with bronzed glam makeup, with blushed cheeks and tinted lips, to add some extra panache to the whole ensemble. Meanwhile, she also added sparkling turquoise earrings that added a pop of color against the darker palette. The whole look was an absolute blessing. Fans online quickly compared Karol’s daring ensemble to a futuristic mermaid-meets-rockstar moment. In fact, many also praised the bold Natalia Fedner creation for pushing red carpet fashion boundaries. The revealing chainmail-inspired top continued the growing celebrity obsession with naked dressing and metallic mesh fashion, proving once again that Karol G never shies away from a headline-making moment. title: Girls head outdoors for a “digital detox” at summer camp - reflector.com
content: THE CENTER SQUARE — In some hamlets of the mountains, the impact of Hurricane He… ASHE COUNTY — Most Carolina West Wireless customers will be … PIEDMONT — Hundreds of girls across western and central North Carolina are gearing up to explore the outdoors at day, overnight and horse summer camp programs with Girl Scouts Carolinas Peaks to Piedmont (GSCP2P). This summer, the overnight week-long and half-week sessions of summer camp programs are hosted at Keyauwee Program Center in Sophia for girls in rising grades 2 to 12. Day camps will be hosted in Greensboro, Hickory and Black Mountain for girls in rising grades 1-5. “Girl Scout summer camp is an amazing opportunity for all girls to explore new possibilities outside of their normal routines,” said Elaine Loyack, Chief Executive Officer at GSCP2P. “At camp, girls can grow their independence and confidence through hands-on learning and make new friends that lift them up in a safe, supportive space.” This year’s theme, Explore More Camp, encourages campers to engage in a variety of activities during their experience and “explore more” than what they normally would do. Programs are full of favorite traditional camp activities like swimming, archery, boating and campfires plus an opportunity to choose from a variety of new sessions like visiting the barn, participating in sports and games, learning new crafting skills and more. This year, all overnight campers will get to enjoy an equestrian experience on site at the Circle C Equestrian Center at no additional cost. Camp is for all girls and Girl Scouts, so they do not have to be a current member to have an exciting summer camp adventure. The GSCP2P council also offers financial assistance so more girls can attend summer camp. After registering for a program and paying the $50 non-refundable deposit, families can access the online financial aid application. In 2025, overnight campers who applied for financial assistance received an average of $280 to use on registration fees. There is still time to reserve a spot to Explore More Camp for a full week or half week session of overnight camp and day camps. Registrations should be complete at least 10 days before the session start date. Visit www.CampLikeAGirl.org to view the 2026 Summer Camp Program Guide and discover all the outdoor summer fun with Girl Scouts. The local council serves over 5,600 girls and 4,400 adult volunteers in 40 counties and maintains three camp properties and four service centers offering unique experiences for girls and adults. title: ASUS ROG Strix GS-BE18000 [Review] – Wi-Fi 7 That Slaps. - G Style Magazine
content: Over the past several weeks, the ASUS ROG Strix GS-BE18000 has become the centerpiece of my home network, handling everything from competitive multiplayer  gaming and nightly livestreams to downloading massive game updates and remote gaming sessions throughout my apartment. My home presents a unique challenge. I live in a pre-war New York City apartment building with thick brick walls that have always been the enemy of strong Wi-Fi coverage. Even high-end routers I’ve tested over the years have struggled to consistently maintain peak speeds from room to room.Computer & Video Games The GS-BE18000, however, brought something genuinely new to the table. Between its Wi-Fi 7 capabilities, Automated Frequency Coordination (AFC), and seamless integration with my existing ASUS ZenWiFi XT9 through AiMesh, it delivered one of the most consistently reliable wireless experiences I’ve had in years. Unlike many gaming routers that resemble futuristic spacecraft covered in antennas, the GS-BE18000 takes a far more refined approach. The compact vertical chassis looks clean enough to blend into a living room while still maintaining the unmistakable ROG aesthetic. The internal antenna design keeps the exterior tidy without sacrificing wireless performance, and the subtle Aura RGB lighting gives it just enough personality without becoming distracting. Build quality is excellent throughout, and incredibly light—could be mistaken as cheaply built, but honestly I think it works well because of the internal bands. Around the back you’ll find one of its biggest strengths: eight 2.5GbE Ethernet ports, making it incredibly easy to build a fully multi-gig home network without immediately needing an additional switch. The GS-BE18000 is a tri-band Wi-Fi 7 router capable of delivering up to 18Gbps of combined theoretical wireless throughput across the 2.4GHz, 5GHz, and 6GHz bands. ASUS pairs that with a quad-core 2.0GHz processor, 2GB of DDR4 memory, and support for the latest Wi-Fi 7 technologies, including 320MHz channels, Multi-Link Operation (MLO), 4K-QAM, OFDMA, MU-MIMO, WPA3 security, and Multi-RU Puncturing. Where this router truly separates itself is its support for Automated Frequency Coordination (AFC). Once enabled, AFC allows the 6GHz radio to operate at Standard Power where supported, significantly improving usable range compared to traditional Low Power Indoor operation. Rather than simply advertising higher theoretical speeds, AFC extends the distance at which those speeds remain available, making 6GHz far more practical throughout an entire home. ASUS also continues to offer one of the strongest software ecosystems in networking. AiProtection Pro, Adaptive QoS, VPN Fusion, Open NAT, Guest Networks, ASUSWRT 5.0, and full AiMesh compatibility are all included without requiring a subscription. The GS-BE18000 has been powering my streaming setup every night while simultaneously handling downloads, smart home devices, and competitive gaming sessions without missing a beat. My desktop remains hardwired through one of the 2.5GbE ports for streaming stability, while much of my testing focused on wireless performance using the ROG Ally X and Strix Scar 18.Computer & Video Games This is where the router genuinely impressed me. With my ASUS ZenWiFi XT9 deployed as an AiMesh node in the second half of my apartment, enabling AFC transformed my experience. Areas that would normally force devices to roam onto weaker signals now maintained excellent throughput, even with multiple brick walls separating me from the primary router. Whether I was grinding games two rooms away on the ROG Ally X or downloading large titles while someone else streamed video, the connection remained remarkably stable. The best way I can describe it is simple: it felt as though the Wi-Fi access point was sitting right beside me regardless of where I was in the apartment. That consistency is something benchmark charts don’t fully capture, but it’s immediately noticeable during everyday use. Gaming performance was equally impressive. Latency remained consistently low, downloads saturated my available internet bandwidth, and I experienced none of the random signal drops or throughput fluctuations that older Wi-Fi generations occasionally introduced in difficult environments.Computer & Video Games My only real limitation isn’t unique to ASUS. To fully benefit from everything this router offers, you’ll need Wi-Fi 7-compatible devices and, ideally, a multi-gig internet connection. Users still relying on Wi-Fi 5 or gigabit networking simply won’t unlock its full potential. AFC is also currently dependent on regional support and proper activation, meaning not every market will immediately benefit from its biggest innovation. The ASUS ROG Strix GS-BE18000 is a very easy router to recommend. Rather than chasing flashy specifications alone, ASUS focused on solving one of Wi-Fi 7’s biggest challenges: making high-speed 6GHz connectivity useful beyond the same room as the router. Combined with AiMesh, an excellent software suite, all-2.5GbE networking, and the real-world advantages of AFC, the GS-BE18000 consistently delivered exceptional performance throughout one of the more challenging wireless environments I’ve tested. title: 4 Korean oil refiners charged with fixing fuel prices before and after start of Iran war - 한겨레
content: Four major Korean oil refiners and top executives are being charged with fixing petroleum prices, and thereby inflating gas prices, despite having adequate crude oil reserves when the US and Israel started bombing Iran on Feb. 28. Prosecutors estimate that the scheme had a total economic impact of 26 trillion won (US$17 billion) On Monday, Na Hui-seok, the prosecutor responsible for fair trade investigations at the Seoul Central District Prosecutors’ Office, announced charges against four Korean oil refiners — HD Hyundai Oilbank, SK Energy Co., GS Caltex Corp. and S-Oil Corp. — for alleged violations of the Monopoly Regulation and Fair Trade Act. Two employees at HD Hyundai Oilbank, including the head of the pricing department, will face trial for swapping information with another refiner to set prices, while the head of domestic sales at GS Caltex is charged with deleting data prior to an inspection by the Fair Trade Commission. “We’ve confirmed that the primary cause [of the soaring prices] was collusion between the executives of the pricing departments at HD Hyundai Oilbank and SK Energy on the timing and amount of their price increases. Since their prices were later matched by GS Caltex and S-Oil, prices in the domestic oil refining market rapidly surged,” prosecutors explained. Prosecutors said that HD Hyundai Oilbank and SK Energy’s price-fixing scheme was worth a record-setting 14.2 trillion won (US$9.3 billion) and that when GS Caltex and S-Oil’s copycat price hikes were taken into consideration, the scheme had a total economic impact of 26 trillion won. The prosecutors maintain that the four refiners had no reason to raise prices as they did because they had ample reserves of crude oil when the US and Israel initiated hostilities against Iran. title: Mr. G’s Pizzeria marks 30 years as friendship preserves legacy | Bryan - College Station - Community Impact
content: As Mr. G’s Pizzeria celebrates three decades in downtown Bryan, owner Susan Carnes reflects on the unlikely friendship preserving the restaurant’s legacy and inspiring its next chapter. For years, customers walking into Mr. G’s Pizzeria in Historic Downtown Bryan were likely to find founder Giovanni “Mr. G” Cerone sitting at a dining room table, paperwork spread out before him as he greeted regulars, welcomed newcomers and shared stories from a life that had taken him from Italy to Texas. Nearly five years after Mr. G's passing, that presence still lingers inside the 30-year-old restaurant. His recipes remain, as do many of the traditions which made the pizzeria a downtown Bryan institution. Now, as the restaurant celebrates its 30th anniversary, the family he chose is carrying his legacy into the business’s next chapter. Mr. G’s Pizzeria will celebrate 30 years in business this month while expanding its footprint with the opening of g’s Southside Italian Cafe in College Station. The new café, expected to open with a soft launch in mid-July before a grand opening this fall, isn’t replacing the downtown restaurant. Instead, owner Susan Carnes described it as “a nod and a tribute” to Mr. G. Carnes wasn’t looking to own a restaurant when she first met Mr. G. She and her husband had just celebrated their 10-year anniversary at Downtown Uncorked, which was located in downtown Bryan until it moved to south College Station in 2021. The couple stopped into Mr. G’s to grab a pizza for their children at home. Instead, Carnes found herself talking with the restaurant’s owner for nearly two hours. “It was like love at first sight, friendship at first sight,” she said with a laugh. “These two families just adopted each other.” “He says–in his little Italian accent–he goes, ‘Susan, if you [don’t] take it, [I’ll] close at the end of the month,’” she recalled him saying. Although she had little restaurant experience beyond waiting tables in college, Carnes and her family stepped in during the uncertainty of the COVID-19 pandemic. Today, her children have grown up inside the business much like several employees who have spent decades there. One longtime pizza cook has worked at Mr. G’s since she was 15 years old, and Carnes’ teenage son will soon bus tables at the new café. Mr. G’s widow Houda remains closely involved and has even shared recipes from her former College Station restaurant, Cenare, for the new concept. Much has changed since Mr. G’s opened in 1996, but the recipes that built its reputation remain largely untouched. The restaurant continues to serve its signature pizzas from classic Margherita and Hawaiian pies to house specialties like the Lu Pizza, which is topped with mozzarella, feta, caramelized onions and prosciutto. The menu also includes calzones, pasta, subs, salads, garlic bread, gluten-free and keto options and desserts like tiramisu and cannoli. At the heart of it all is the pizza dough recipe Mr. G. brought to Bryan decades ago. Today, Carnes said only two people know how to make it. While the downtown pizzeria will continue serving its signature and longtime favorites, the new café will expand on the family’s Italian roots. The kitchen at the College Station location will also become the primary location for preparing dough, sauces and other ingredients used by both restaurants. Despite the expansion, Carnes said Bryan remains home. She calls the downtown restaurant a “7,000 square-foot elephant” that has survived recessions, COVID-19 and decades of changing restaurant trends. “It would leave a hole in the heart,” she said. “So, as long as we’re able, Mr. G’s downtown Bryan will be [here].” The restaurant continues to draw crowds during First Friday events, hosts live entertainment and private events and remains one of downtown Bryan’s long-running eateries. For Carnes, opening another restaurant isn’t about growing a brand nearly as much as preserving a friendship. The lowercase “g” in g’s Southside Italian Cafe was intentional, she said, as it’s not meant to replace or compete with Mr. G’s. Carnes told Community Impact Mr G’s plans to have specials and parties to celebrate 30 years. In the meantime, Mr. G’s will operate during normal business hours, staying open until 9 p.m. during the week and 10 p.m. on Fridays and Saturdays. title: GS Group Builds Asia's Largest AI Data Center in Donghae - 조선일보
content: 120-trillion-won project in Donghae to reach 2.4GW by 2029, positioning Gangwon as AI hub GS Group is building Asia’s largest AI data center in Donghae, Gangwon Province. It is a mega-project with a maximum investment of 120 trillion Korean won, to be developed to a scale of 2.4GW by 2029. Amid a global surge in demand for data centers due to AI expansion, Gangwon Province has moved to establish itself as a hub for AI infrastructure. Gangwon Province, Donghae City, and GS Group signed a business agreement on the 6th at a small meeting room in the Gangwon Provincial Government Office to establish the ‘Donghae AI Data Center Campus.’ Those attending the agreement ceremony included Gangwon Governor Woo Sang-ho, Donghae Mayor Lee Jeong-hak, GS Vice Chairman Hong Soon-gi, and GS E&R Representative Hwang Byeong-so. The Donghae AI Data Center will be built on approximately 70,000 pyeong of land within the Bukpyeong Second General Industrial Complex in Donghae City. The plan is to first construct 1.2GW by 2028, then add another 1.2GW by 2029 to complete a total scale of 2.4GW. As a single AI data center, it will be the largest in Asia. GS announced the plan to build the Donghae AI Data Center at the ‘National Report Meeting on the Three Mega Projects for Korea’s Great Leap Forward’ on the 29th of last month. The total investment cost is 30 trillion Korean won, and including costs for graphics processing units (GPUs) and memory, it is expected to reach up to 120 trillion Korean won. The project site, the Bukpyeong Second General Industrial Complex, is an industrial complex that GS began construction on in 2016 and completed in 2022. With the site already secured and power supply conditions in place, the project is expected to proceed swiftly. Measures to secure power and water, the core elements of an AI data center, have also been prepared. The 1.2GW-scale facility to be built by 2028 will receive power linked to GS Donghae Power’s power generation facilities. The cooling system will operate using an immersion cooling method, where servers are submerged in special cooling oil, and approximately 1,100 tons of industrial water per day. Gangwon Province plans to operate a fast-track system for permits and licenses to allow companies to focus on investment, and actively support infrastructure such as power and water supply. Governor Woo’s first official order upon taking office on the 1st to form the ‘AI Data Center Promotion Team’ was also aimed at accelerating the project. This agreement is significant as it marks the realization of Governor Woo’s vision for fostering the AI industry, which he revealed in an interview with this newspaper last week. At the time, Governor Woo disclosed that alongside GS’s 2.4GW project in Donghae, SK Group is also pushing to build a 1GW-scale AI data center in the Gangwon region. If SK’s project proceeds, Gangwon Province could become the country’s largest AI infrastructure cluster with a total of 3.4GW-scale AI data centers. Globally, competition to secure AI data centers is intensifying. McKinsey & Company, a global consulting firm, projected that while demand for AI data centers will grow by 19–22% annually, supply will lag, leading to a shortage of approximately 15GW in the U.S. alone by 2030. Consequently, global companies are expanding AI infrastructure investments to regions outside the U.S. Gangwon Province highlights its strengths: abundant power supply, vast industrial land, and relatively fewer location restrictions. AI data centers are power-intensive industries that consume far more electricity than general data centers, giving regions capable of large-scale power supply a competitive edge. The capital region faces difficulties in adding large-scale AI data centers due to saturated power grids. Gangwon Governor Woo Sang-ho stated, “AI data centers are the core infrastructure of the AI industry and the growth foundation that will determine future industrial competitiveness. The Donghae AI Data Center will be the starting point for building Gangwon’s AI industry ecosystem and a key hub for enhancing South Korea’s AI industry competitiveness.”

title: South Korean prosecutors indict four major refiners over allegations of oil price collusion - CNBC
content:
South Korean prosecutors on Monday indicted four major domestic oil refiners for violating fair trade laws, alleging they colluded to drive up domestic fuel prices following the Middle East conflict. HD Hyundai Oilbank, SK Energy, GS Caltex, and S-Oil were the four companies that breached the nation’s fair trade act, according to Yonhap News Agency. HD Hyundai Oilbank and SK Energy colluded on 14.2 trillion won ($9.2 billion) worth of oil sales, Yonhap reported, citing prosecutors. Factoring in GS Caltex and S-Oil, which allegedly mimicked those prices, the total anticompetitive impact stands at roughly 26 trillion won, the report said. The investigation was initiated after domestic oil prices sharply rose following the U.S.–Iran conflict, prosecutors said, finding that collusion by pricing executives at two of the firms over the timing and scale of the hikes was the primary driver. The prosecution said the collusion was not a standalone incident but a long-standing, systemic practice that surfaced during a time of global crisis.
